title: Nectar Demo Reading List
description: Sample content used to generate Nectar's App Store and README screenshots. Original placeholder text.

items.title: A Quiet Kind of Orbit
items.summary: Two officers, one observation lounge, and a night watch neither of them planned to spend alone.
items.content_html:
The night watch on Deck 5 was the quietest four hours of Kirk's week, and lately he'd started finding reasons to spend most of them in the observation lounge instead of his quarters, where the stars did the talking and he didn't have to.

Spock found him there more often than either of them ever planned. "Command was easier," Spock had once told him, "when you stopped mistaking silence for absence." Kirk hadn't understood it then. He was starting to now.

Tonight Spock arrived with two cups of something that was technically tea, set one down within Kirk's reach, and took the seat across from him without a word. Outside the viewport, a nebula unspooled itself in slow orange light, indifferent to rank or deadlines or anything else that mattered at 0300 hours.

"You are off duty," Spock said eventually, not quite a question.

"So are you."

"Indeed." A pause, the kind Kirk had learned to wait out rather than fill. "I find I prefer this particular use of the time."

Kirk looked over at him, really looked, the way he rarely let himself in daylight with a bridge full of witnesses, and decided that whatever this was, he preferred it too. Some things didn't need a report filed. Some things just needed the room to keep happening.

items.title: Letters Home
items.summary: An exchange of messages between a cadet and the sister who kept every one of them.
items.content_html:
Dear Maren, the food here is better than I expected and the sleep is worse. Everyone talks about the stars as if they were scenery. Nobody warns you that they are also a kind of homesickness.

I passed the navigation exam. The instructor said my margins were narrow but my instincts were good, which I am choosing to hear as praise.

Write back when you can. Tell me about the garden.

items.title: The Command Track
items.summary: A young lieutenant learns what the captain's chair costs, one small decision at a time.
items.content_html:
Nobody had told Lieutenant Ashe that command was mostly waiting. Waiting for reports, waiting for the right moment to speak, waiting for the small uncomfortable silence that meant someone else was about to say what she already knew.

She had expected drama. What she got was a long corridor and a shorter list of options, and the quiet certainty that either choice would matter to someone she would never meet.

items.title: Sickbay Politics
items.summary: The doctor has opinions about the new regulations. The doctor always has opinions.
items.content_html:
"I am a doctor, not a filing clerk," McCoy said, for what Nurse Chapel calculated was the fourth time that shift, and slid the form back across the desk with two fingers, as though it might be contagious.

The form did not move. Forms rarely did. It sat there, patient and unbothered, waiting for him to run out of adjectives.

items.title: Vulcan Mathematics
items.summary: A short study of how a very logical mind counts the things that cannot be counted.
items.content_html:
There were, Spock reflected, exactly four hundred and twelve tiles on the floor of the science lab, and he had counted them twice, which was once more than logic required and exactly as many times as the afternoon seemed to need.

It was not anxiety. Vulcans did not experience anxiety. It was, he decided, thoroughness applied to an unusually stubborn variable.

items.title: Shore Leave, Interrupted
items.summary: A planet built for relaxation, and a crew that has never once managed to relax on it.
items.content_html:
The beach was perfect, which should have been the first warning. The sand was warm, the water was clear, and somewhere behind the tree line a small white rabbit checked its pocket watch and hurried past without so much as a glance.

"Nobody," Kirk said, lowering his sunglasses, "mention it."

items.title: Ten Forward, After Hours
items.summary: Long after the last shift, the lounge belongs to the people who cannot quite bring themselves to leave.
items.content_html: By midnight ship's time the lounge had thinned to three tables, one bartender, and a very quiet android who was, by his own account, not lingering. He was observing. There was a difference, he had explained, though nobody had asked.

items.title: Promenade Hours
items.summary: Business, gossip, and one very persistent rumor about the replicator on Level Two.
items.content_html:
The Promenade woke the way it always did: shutters rattling up, a dozen languages beginning at once, and somewhere in the middle of it Quark already complaining about margins.

It was, Odo thought, the closest thing to a heartbeat the station had, and he would have denied enjoying it under oath.
